_note: 1.6.1 (Batch D, N6) campus phases: what the campus and its key people are busy with during a stretch of the year. Each phase is {"id", "from": "M5 W1 Mon", "to": "M5 W2 Fri", "line": "one line for <now>"}; every year, inclusive. The engine puts the active phase's line into <now> (stepCampusEvents, $ui.phase). 2.1.1 (owner-approved planning/DRAFT_campus_phases.md, roadmap R3): the days before and after the calendar's events; one at a time (no overlaps), no NPC names (they repeat every year), none on a home, lockdown or away day, none while {{user}} is away from campus; never what the event line, lore 134, the exam-week moods or the place lines in merge_lorebooks.py PHASES already say. tools/gen_engine.py checks all of it. trends (2.1.1, owner: 'something more mundane from real campus life, a food that goes viral for a week'): weekly fads for the days without a phase; {id, season ('all' or a list), line}; a week has one at trend_rate percent (seeded per chat and week, engine trendOn), never one of the last trend_gap weeks'; <now> labels it 'Campus fad this week' and lets people take to it or scoff in character. Items they name are data/shop.json items. Text only: no price or stock changes.

phases.line: The first weeks: first-years still lose their way between buildings, the first homework is landing, and the clubs are settling in the members they signed up.
Star Night is on Saturday: students borrow tents and bedrolls, argue over the best spot on the hills, and decide what to wish for at the midnight shower.
The Warding Rite is on Friday: Mystic students who ward or seal rehearse with the staff, and first-years wonder what casting together with hundreds will feel like.
The Creature Studies Expedition goes out on Wednesday of Week 3: kits, boots and field notes are being packed, and the talk is of what lives in Grade III country.
Midterms start next Monday: study groups claim every table, notes are copied and swapped, and the clubs and evenings out quietly empty.
The Club Festival opens on Friday: every club is building its stand and planning demonstrations and samples, and canvassing for gold coins it cannot vote for itself.
The Dorm Competition is this weekend: the qualifiers are the talk of every dorm, and their dorm-mates cheer them on, scout their rivals and give advice nobody asked for.
Crowning Day is on Tuesday: students form their groups of four for the capital, plan what to see and buy in Avalon, and remind each other to change points into coin the day before.
The End of Semester exams start next Monday: the library and study rooms stay full late, tempers are short, and the semester's last free evenings go to revision.
The exams are over and the results and the Dorm Ranking come out on Friday: everyone replays their answers, and the dorms argue about where they will place.
The Mid-Year Break starts next week: most students are writing home and packing trunks; the few staying at Halvard over the break say little about it.
Sports Day is on Saturday of Week 3, with magic banned outright: sign-ups are open, the sport clubs train their favourites, and the strongest mages are teased about running on their own legs.
The Academy Competition starts on Wednesday: the cross-dorm teams of four drill together, and everyone has a guess which team will go on to represent Halvard.
The Thinning comes in Week 3: the staff walk the wards and stock the dorms for a week indoors, the Acting Warden is rarely seen, and those who were here on the breach night go quiet when it comes up.
The Thinning is over and the doors are open again: students trade what they heard through the windows during the lockdown, and most of it grows in the telling.
The Traveling Circus arrives on Thursday of Week 2 and the Academy Showcase follows: posters are up, acts rehearse in every free room, and family visits are being planned, and dreaded.
Midterms start next Monday: the study groups are back, and anyone who earned a Science Fair score is quietly glad to skip the written Magic Theory paper.
The Academy Bazaar opens on Thursday: students count their savings, trade rumours of what the foreign traders will bring, and swear they will not spend it all.
Founder Day is on Saturday: talk turns to the treasure hunt nobody has finished in years, last year's clues are argued over, and groups quietly form.
Halvard's team is at the Kingdom Competition in the capital this week; at Halvard classes go on, and any news from the Royal Arena goes round fast.
The Student Council election is next week: both nominees already sit on the Council, and students are making up their minds before the campaign starts.
The Harvest Festival starts on Friday, the last loud thing before the exams: costumes are being sewn, stalls and haunted corridors planned, and nobody mentions the exams the week after.

trends.line: Everyone wants Salaffian flatbread: the queue at The Salaffian Oven runs out of the door at lunch, and anyone who has not tried one yet is told they must.
Nightwell's honey cream coffee is the drink of the moment: cups appear in every classroom, and the line before first period has become a place to be seen.
In the heat everyone carries a Nightwell iced coffee, and being seen without one has somehow become a statement.
The bakery's Blossom honey cake sells out before noon every day, and students trade tips on when the next tray comes out.
The bakery's spiced apple turnovers are the autumn obsession: people time their walk past the Mall to catch them hot.
Roasted chestnuts are the thing: a paper cone in every cold hand, and a running argument over which café roasts them best.
Nightwell's hot chocolate with cream is everywhere; study groups have started meeting there just for it.
Iced fruit coolers are the summer fix; the cafés have started naming flavours after the dorms, and every dorm insists its own is best.
The Sunfizz bottle hunt is on: students collect empties for the two-point return, and a few corridors have quietly become someone's territory.
A rumour says the Cooking Club's honey bread brings luck before a test: the Saturday bake sells out, and the club pretends not to be pleased.
Dragonchess fever: the living boards are never free, unofficial ladders are chalked up in the common rooms, and losing streaks are taken personally.
A new card game played with gilt-edged cards has swept the dorms; everyone claims to know the real rules, and nobody agrees what they are.
Juggling has caught on: balls and beanbags fly in the courtyards between classes, with the occasional apology when one lands where it should not.
Everyone is learning a vanishing-coin trick done by hand alone, and anyone caught using magic to cheat at it is not forgiven.
A song from the afternoon broadcast is stuck in everyone's head: someone hums it in every corridor, and the Announcement Room is begged to stop playing it, or to play it again.
Small plush animals from Pennywhistle Curios have started hanging from satchels, and whose plush is whose has become a small map of who is close to whom.
Black silk ribbons are the fashion, tied on wrists and satchels, and the Etiquette teachers have opinions about what counts as uniform.
Merryhew's colour-change hair sweets are the dare of the week: every class has someone with alarming hair, and the game is to keep a straight face.
Anonymous kind notes keep appearing on the Notice Board, one for someone new each morning; everyone wants to know who writes them, and who is next.
Early-morning running has become a thing: before breakfast the paths round the lake fill with students who will have given up by next week.
A study method is going round: an hourglass on the table, work until the sand runs out, then a short break; hourglasses have gone missing from every lab.
The Mall's game halls have a new favourite game, free hours vanish there, and waiting in the queue to play is half the fun.
